question.text: Under the PML Rules, small accounts can only be opened at branches that are linked to which system, to ensure compliance with balance and transaction limits?

answer.text: Any branch of a scheduled commercial bank
Core Banking Solution (CBS) linked branches or branches where manual monitoring is possible
Only metropolitan branches with dedicated AML officers
Only designated branches approved by FIU-IND

explanation.text: The Logic: A small account shall be opened only at Core Banking Solution (CBS) linked branches of a banking company, or at a branch where it is possible to manually monitor and ensure that foreign remittances are not credited to the account and that the stipulated monthly and annual aggregate transaction and balance limits are not breached. The Trap: "Any branch" is too broad and "only metro branches" / "only FIU-IND designated branches" are fabricated restrictions. The Rules require either CBS linkage or branch-level manual monitoring capability. Note: The CBS-linked branch or manual-monitoring requirement is grounded in the checked workbook page; the precise monthly and annual aggregate limits applicable to small accounts should be confirmed against the current PML Rules.
